'''Magori''' is a nearly extinct [[Austronesian languages|Austronesian]] language of [[Papua New Guinea]] that has been strongly restructured through contact with neighboring [[Papuan languages]], perhaps [[Mailu language|Mailu]], which the Magori people speak fluently today. The restructuring was so extensive that Magori's family was long in doubt; it was finally established by Dutton in 1976.<ref>William Foley, 1986, ''The Papuan Languages of New Guinea'', p. 283</ref> Mailu (also called Magi) in turn borrowed large numbers of Austronesian words, either from Magori or its extinct Oumic relatives.
